subject: Data residency & safeguards — NovusHealth RFP: export controls and KMS evidence
messages:
From: Lauren Mitchell <lauren.mitchell@novushealth.com>

Cc: Eliot Park <eliot.park@novushealth.com>, procurement@novushealth.com
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: NovusHealth RFP — follow-up: data residency and cross-border safeguards

Jordan —

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement and legal are working through the RFP and we have a small set of follow-up items specific to cross-border data transfers and key management. I attached the spreadsheet with our tracking questions (column B has the specific question IDs). High level: we need confirmation of which infrastructure components may result in EU->US transfer of personal data, the legal basis you rely on, and whether you can provide a DPA annex with specific subprocessor routing rules.

Can someone on your team provide a short narrative on: 1) how Redwood treats customer-uploaded patient/contact data in transit and at rest across regions, 2) whether the hosted API may ever route inference requests to another region for failover, and 3) a diagram of KMS/HSM custody for customer keys for private deployments?

We'd like answers by EOD next Wednesday (Aug 26) to slot into our vendor review.

Regards,
Lauren Mitchell
Senior Sourcing Manager
NovusHealth

Attachment: novus_rfi_questions.xlsx (spreadsheet, 12KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Wed, 25 Aug 2026 08:57:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: NovusHealth RFP — follow-up: data residency and cross-border safeguards

Lauren —

Attached is a consolidated response pack: we filled the workbook with row-level answers and included two supporting artifacts (KMS custody diagram and a proposed DPA annex redline for the subprocessor routing section). Highlights:

1) Data handling (hosted API & Dedicated):
- Inference requests to the hosted API are routed to a customer-configured primary region by default; we do not proactively re-route live requests to another region unless a configured failover policy triggers (customer can opt-out). When failover occurs, token-level metadata indicates region of execution and request identifiers are logged centrally.
- For Dedicated and Private deployments (VPC / on-prem), customer data stays within the allocated region and is not routed externally unless explicitly configured for cross-region replication.

2) Legal basis & transfers:
- For EU customers using the hosted API, exports to the US are scoped under our DPF mapping. We offer model variants pinned to EU regions for customers requiring data residency. For transfers from EU to US, we provide an implementation of SCCs via our DPA annex and technical controls mapping (attached).

3) KMS / key custody:
- Hosted: Customer-managed keys via KMS integrations (AWS KMS / GCP Cloud KMS) supported for Dedicated and Private. For hosted accounts opting for Redwood-managed keys, keys are stored within our HSM-backed service and access is strictly role-scoped; we log all key usage and provide key rotation reports on request. See attached 'redwood_kms_diagram_v2.pdf'.

4) Evidence & audit:
- We can provide export control logs, per-request region tags, SOC 2 type II report snippets, and sample DPA annex redlines. We included a redline with suggested subprocessor routing language.

Next steps: please confirm if you want the DPA annex redline as-is or if your counsel prefers tracked changes in Word. If acceptable, we can move to a short remote session next week with your privacy counsel to walk through the annex.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: dpa_annex_proposed_changes.docx (Word redline, 48KB), redwood_kms_diagram_v2.pdf (diagram, 160KB)

From: Eliot Park <eliot.park@novushealth.com>

Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: NovusHealth RFP — follow-up: data residency and cross-border safeguards

Marissa / Jordan —

Thank you for the prompt and thorough package. I reviewed the KMS diagram and the annex redline. A couple of small asks from legal:

- Can you add a short statement confirming that for Redwood-managed keys we will receive access logs in a machine-readable format (CSV/JSON) and the retention period for those logs?
- For the annex: please clarify the subprocessor routing clause to explicitly state that when a failover to a secondary region is triggered for the hosted API, only ephemeral inference metadata (no raw customer-uploaded payloads) may be temporarily routed, unless customer has enabled cross-region replication. This is important for our internal risk team.

If you can add those clarifications we should be able to move to contract review. Can we do a 30-minute call on Thu 08/27 to finalize?

—Eliot
Eliot Park
Privacy Counsel
NovusHealth
